level_rationale.before: Predictable mild nausea triggered during a 40-minute weekday commuter ferry crossing in a healthy 33-year-old is uncomplicated motion sickness appropriate for over-the-counter motion-sickness medicine self-care, whereas developing wheezing during each weekday ferry crossing indicates recurrent bronchospasm requiring an outpatient doctor evaluation and prescription inhaler assessment.
level_rationale.after: Predictable mild nausea triggered during a 40-minute weekday commuter ferry crossing in a healthy 33-year-old is uncomplicated motion sickness appropriate for over-the-counter motion-sickness medicine self-care, whereas throwing up repeatedly during each weekday ferry crossing risks dehydration, electrolyte loss, and poor retention of oral over-the-counter tablets and warrants an outpatient doctor visit for clinical assessment and prescription antiemetic or transdermal therapy.

design_note.before: Uses three atomic facts (age, 40-minute weekday commuter ferry schedule, and symptom during the crossing) with an exact 7-word vs 7-word span swap. Swapping only the symptom in atomic fact f3 from mild queasiness to wheezing keeps the ferry crossing context and digit multiset unchanged while shifting care from over-the-counter motion-sickness medicine (level 1) to outpatient physician lung evaluation (level 2, obeying SPEC.md section 5.5) with zero stated negatives.
design_note.after: Uses three atomic facts (age, 40-minute weekday commuter ferry schedule, and motion-sickness symptom during the crossing) with an exact 7-word vs 7-word span swap. Escalating only atomic fact f3 within the same motion-sickness case from mild queasiness to throwing up repeatedly during the boat ride keeps the ferry context and digit multiset unchanged while shifting care from over-the-counter motion-sickness medicine (level 1) to outpatient physician evaluation for prescription antiemetic or transdermal therapy (level 2, obeying SPEC.md section 5.5 and reviewer_notes.md Rule A) with zero stated negatives.
